title: White Paper - Part 4 of 4 - Energy-Flow Cosmology, Part 4: Regime Susceptibility and Cross-Scale Mapping
description: Introduces a regime susceptibility function T(S) that maps the SPARC-calibrated coupling at galactic scales to a cosmological amplitude without new parameters. Shows that β(S)·ρeff(S) is constant, yielding exact self‑regulation, GR recovery as S→0, and a parameter‑free prediction for the amplification βcosm/βgal≈6.25 alongside dynamical dark energy w(a)≠−1 testable by Euclid.
keywords: dark matter and dark energy phases

entropic_phases.latex: \nabla_{\mu} J^{\mu} = \begin{cases} < 0 & \text{convergent flow \;\Rightarrow\; excess gravity (DM regime)} \\ = 0 & \text{equilibrium (matter-dominated)} \\ > 0 & \text{divergent flow \;\Rightarrow\; accelerated expansion (DE regime)} \end{cases}
entropic_phases.description: Defines dark matter and dark energy as convergent and divergent phases of a single energy‑flow current along entropy gradients.

rho_eff.description: Effective energy density available for dynamical exchange; vanishes at S→0 and S→1 and peaks at S=1/2.

pressure_divergence.description: Effective pressure is set by the divergence of the energy‑flow current; divergent flow yields negative pressure.

w_of_a.description: Leading-order effective equation of state linking background dynamics to the regime‑scaled coupling.

T_of_S.description: Regime susceptibility mapping the effective coupling strength across the entropic continuum relative to a reference regime S0.

beta_of_S.description: Cross‑scale mapping from the SPARC‑calibrated galactic coupling β0 at S0 to its cosmological value at S.

self_regulation.description: Exact self‑regulation: the product of regime susceptibility and effective energy density is constant, enforcing GR recovery at S→0 and de Sitter approach as S→1.

omega_ratio_mapping.description: Relates the observed DE-to-matter ratio to location on the entropic continuum rather than a fundamental constant.

key_results.main_finding: A parameter-free regime susceptibility T(S) maps galactic-scale coupling to cosmological strength, yielding self-regulation (β·ρeff=const), GR recovery at S→0, and a concrete amplification prediction βcosm/βgal≈6.25 with dynamical w(a)≠−1.

sealed_predictions.statement: Amplification of the coupling between galactic and cosmological regimes is parameter-free with β_cosm/β_gal ≈ 6.25 implied by T(S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint inference of β0 from SPARC and β_cosm (or w0) from Planck+BAO+SNe and Euclid/DESI expansion data.

sealed_predictions.statement: Dark energy is dynamical with w(z) ≠ −1; leading-order prediction w(a) = −β(S) a with w0 ≈ −1 set by Scosm.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Euclid and Rubin LSST tomographic constraints on w0, wa (and w(z)) over 0 < z ≲ 2.

sealed_predictions.statement: Self-regulation holds exactly: β(S)·S(1−S) is constant across redshift.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Consistency tests combining growth (fσ8, S8, Σ, R) with background expansion to recover β(S) and ρeff(S) as functions of z.

sealed_predictions.statement: No new fields or free amplitudes are required to connect galactic and cosmological scales once T(S) is applied.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Global fits that require additional free parameters beyond β0 and the S-based mapping to match both galaxy rotation curves and cosmology.

kill_criteria: KC1: Euclid+Rubin find w(z) consistent with −1 (e.g., w0 = −1 and wa = 0 within uncertainties across 0 < z ≲ 1.5), ruling out the predicted dynamical w(a) ≠ −1.
KC2: The empirically inferred amplification between regimes is incompatible with β_cosm/β_gal ≈ 6.25 (from independent β0 at S0≈0.1 and cosmological w0), falsifying the T(S) mapping.
KC3: Combined background and growth data show redshift dependence in the product β(S)·S(1−S) inconsistent with a constant, violating self-regulation.
KC4: Early-universe probes (e.g., CMB anisotropies, BBN) detect departures from GR attributable to non-vanishing effective coupling as S→0, contradicting exact GR recovery.

KC5: A successful joint fit to galactic dynamics and cosmological observables demonstrably requires introducing new fields or independent coupling parameters beyond β0 and S, contradicting the parameter-free cross-scale mapping.
